items.story:
Citizens for Justice and Peace, a human rights organization, has urged the Indian government to immediately honour its promises after protesters were detained across the country, particularly in Assam, West Bengal, and Bihar. The call comes in response to the recent arrests of protesters who were demonstrating against the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test, or NEET, a standardized test for medical college admissions. The organization has expressed concern over the crackdown on peaceful protesters and has demanded that the government take immediate action to release those detained. The situation has sparked widespread concern among human rights activists and the general public.

The recent developments are part of a larger controversy surrounding the NEET exam, which has been a subject of debate and protests in India. The exam has been criticized for being biased towards students from certain socio-economic backgrounds, and many have called for its abolition. The protests have been ongoing for several weeks, with students and activists demanding that the government reconsider its decision to implement the exam. The government has maintained that the exam is necessary to ensure fairness and transparency in medical college admissions, but the opposition has argued that it is unfair and discriminatory.

According to reports, several protesters were detained by the police in Assam, West Bengal, and Bihar, with many being charged with various offenses. The Citizens for Justice and Peace has alleged that the crackdown on protesters is a clear violation of their right to freedom of expression and assembly. The organization has demanded that the government withdraw the cases against the protesters and release those detained immediately. The Indian government has not commented on the matter, but officials have maintained that the police action was necessary to maintain law and order.

The arrests have sparked widespread outrage among students, activists, and the general public, with many taking to social media to express their solidarity with the protesters. The opposition parties have also criticized the government's handling of the situation, with many calling for the release of the detained protesters. The situation has also drawn attention from human rights organizations, which have expressed concern over the government's actions. The United Nations has also been approached by human rights activists to intervene in the matter and ensure that the rights of the protesters are protected.

The controversy surrounding the NEET exam and the subsequent crackdown on protesters has wider implications for the country. The incident has highlighted the growing dissatisfaction among students and activists with the government's policies, particularly with regards to education. The situation has also raised questions about the freedom of expression and assembly in India, with many arguing that the government is becoming increasingly authoritarian. The incident has also sparked concerns about the impact on the country's democratic institutions and the rule of law.

As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen how the government will respond to the demands of the protesters and the Citizens for Justice and Peace. The organization has warned that it will take legal action if the government fails to honour its promises and release the detained protesters. The incident has also raised questions about the future of the NEET exam and the government's policies on education. With the situation continuing to simmer, it is likely that the controversy will continue to dominate the headlines in the coming days, and the government will be under increasing pressure to find a solution to the crisis.

items.headline: France's leaders find themselves drawn to the legacy of wartime hero Charles de Gaulle.
items.teaser: French politicians are increasingly invoking the legacy of Charles de Gaulle, the country's former president, as a way to connect with vo…
items.story:
French politicians are increasingly invoking the legacy of Charles de Gaulle, the country's former president, as a way to connect with voters and bolster their own credibility. De Gaulle, who served as president from 1959 to 1969, is widely regarded as a unifying figure in French politics, and his name has become synonymous with French exceptionalism and independence. In recent months, several high-profile politicians have referenced de Gaulle in speeches and interviews, highlighting his commitment to French sovereignty and his role in shaping the country's post-war identity. This trend is particularly notable among conservative and nationalist politicians, who see de Gaulle as a symbol of traditional French values.

The appeal of de Gaulle's legacy can be traced back to his pivotal role in modern French history, particularly during World War II, when he led the Free French Forces against Nazi occupation. After the war, de Gaulle played a key role in shaping the country's constitution and establishing the Fifth Republic, which has endured to this day. His presidency was marked by a strong emphasis on French independence and a commitment to maintaining the country's global influence, values that continue to resonate with many French voters. As a result, de Gaulle's name has become a powerful symbol of French patriotism and national pride, making him an attractive reference point for politicians seeking to tap into these sentiments.

According to recent polls, a significant majority of French voters view de Gaulle as one of the country's greatest leaders, and his legacy continues to be widely studied and debated in academic and political circles. Politicians such as Marine Le Pen and Eric Zemmour have been particularly vocal in their admiration for de Gaulle, citing his commitment to French sovereignty and his willingness to challenge the status quo. Official statements from these politicians have emphasized the need for a renewed focus on French identity and independence, values that they argue are essential to the country's future prosperity and security. Experts note that this rhetoric is likely intended to appeal to voters who feel disillusioned with the current political establishment and are seeking a more assertive and patriotic leadership style.

The invocation of de Gaulle's legacy has sparked a range of reactions from stakeholders and the public, with some hailing it as a welcome return to traditional French values and others criticizing it as a nostalgic and divisive tactic. Some commentators have argued that the emphasis on de Gaulle's legacy is a cynical attempt to exploit voter nostalgia and distract from more pressing issues, such as economic inequality and social injustice. Meanwhile, others see it as a genuine effort to reconnect with France's rich history and cultural heritage, and to promote a more confident and assertive national identity. As the country prepares for upcoming elections, it remains to be seen how this trend will play out and whether it will have a significant impact on the outcome.

The wider context of this development is closely tied to the ongoing debates about European integration, immigration, and national identity that are taking place across the continent. As France and other European countries grapple with the challenges of globalization and cultural diversity, the appeal of de Gaulle's legacy can be seen as part of a broader backlash against the perceived erosion of national sovereignty and traditional values. This trend is not unique to France, as similar debates are taking place in countries such as Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom, where politicians are also seeking to tap into voter concerns about identity and belonging. As the European Union continues to evolve and face new challenges, the legacy of de Gaulle and other European leaders is likely to remain a key point of reference in these debates.

As the French political landscape continues to evolve, it remains to be seen how the invocation of de Gaulle's legacy will play out in the long term. Upcoming elections and policy debates will provide a key test of whether this trend is a lasting phenomenon or a fleeting moment of nostalgia. Meanwhile, experts will be watching closely to see how the legacy of de Gaulle is used and interpreted by different politicians and stakeholders, and what implications this may have for France's relationships with its European partners and the wider world. As the country navigates the complexities of the 21st century, the enduring appeal of de Gaulle's legacy is likely to remain a significant factor in shaping French politics and identity.

The wider context to this development is the ongoing crackdown on democratic freedoms in Hong Kong. The outcome of Wu's case is still uncertain, and it remains to be seen whether the UK government will reverse its decision to deport him. items.story:
Many South Asian immigrants who arrived in the United Kingdom in the latter half of the 20th century have credited early South Asian television and radio programmes with helping them settle into their new lives. These programmes, which included music and practical tips, played a significant role in easing the transition for thousands of people who left their homes in search of better opportunities. The programmes provided a sense of comfort and familiarity, allowing immigrants to connect with their cultural heritage while navigating the challenges of living in a new country. As a result, they became an essential part of the daily routine for many South Asian families in the UK.

The history of South Asian programming in the UK dates back to the 1960s, when the BBC first began broadcasting programmes targeted at the growing South Asian community. These early programmes were largely music-based, featuring popular artists and traditional music from India, Pakistan, and other South Asian countries. Over time, the programming expanded to include news, current affairs, and lifestyle shows, all of which were designed to cater to the specific needs and interests of the South Asian community. The programmes were widely popular, not only among South Asian immigrants but also among other communities in the UK who were interested in learning about different cultures.

According to data from the BBC, the number of South Asian programmes increased significantly during the 1970s and 1980s, with many shows being broadcast in languages such as Hindi, Urdu, and Punjabi. The programmes were not only entertaining but also informative, providing viewers with practical tips on how to navigate the complexities of British life. Many of the shows were produced in collaboration with South Asian community groups, ensuring that the content was relevant and responsive to the needs of the community. Official statements from the BBC have acknowledged the importance of these programmes in promoting cultural diversity and social cohesion in the UK.

The impact of South Asian programming on the community has been widely acknowledged, with many people crediting the programmes with helping them feel more at home in the UK. The programmes have also played a significant role in promoting cross-cultural understanding and exchange, allowing people from different backgrounds to learn about and appreciate each other's customs and traditions. Stakeholders, including community leaders and policymakers, have praised the programmes for their contribution to social cohesion and community building. The programmes have also had a positive impact on the British media landscape, paving the way for greater diversity and representation in broadcasting.

The success of South Asian programming in the UK has also had wider implications, with many other countries looking to replicate similar models. In recent years, there has been a growing recognition of the importance of diverse programming in promoting social cohesion and cultural exchange. The UK's experience in this area has been cited as a model for other countries, with many broadcasters and policymakers seeking to learn from the UK's approach to promoting diversity and inclusion in broadcasting. The growth of global media platforms has also created new opportunities for South Asian programming to reach a wider audience, both in the UK and around the world.

As the UK's South Asian community continues to grow and evolve, there are likely to be new challenges and opportunities for programming that caters to their needs. With the rise of digital media and online platforms, there are many new ways for South Asian programmes to reach their audience, and for new voices and perspectives to be heard. As broadcasters and policymakers look to the future, they will need to consider how to build on the successes of the past while also responding to the changing needs and preferences of the South Asian community. This will require a continued commitment to promoting diversity and inclusion in broadcasting, as well as a willingness to innovate and adapt to new technologies and platforms.

items.headline: Most people would opt for a guaranteed £50,000 over the possibility of a £1 million windfall.
items.teaser: A recent survey has found that the vast majority of people, particularly women, would choose a guaranteed £50,000 over a one in ten chanc…
items.story:
A recent survey has found that the vast majority of people, particularly women, would choose a guaranteed £50,000 over a one in ten chance of winning £1 million. The results of the survey, which polled a large and diverse group of individuals, suggest that many people prefer the certainty of a smaller sum of money to the uncertainty of a larger one. This preference for certainty over chance is a common phenomenon in economics and psychology, and has significant implications for how people make financial decisions. The survey's findings are consistent with previous research on risk aversion and decision-making under uncertainty.

The survey's results are not surprising, given the well-documented tendency for people to be risk-averse when it comes to financial decisions. This means that people tend to prefer outcomes that are certain, even if they are not as desirable, to outcomes that are uncertain, even if they have the potential to be more rewarding. This preference for certainty is thought to be driven by a variety of factors, including loss aversion, which is the tendency to fear losses more than gains. The survey's findings are also consistent with research on the role of emotions in decision-making, which suggests that people's financial decisions are often driven by feelings such as fear and anxiety.

According to the survey, a significant majority of respondents, approximately 80%, chose the guaranteed £50,000 over the chance of winning £1 million. This preference for certainty was even more pronounced among women, with over 90% of female respondents choosing the guaranteed sum. The survey also found that the preference for certainty decreased with age, with younger respondents more likely to choose the chance of winning £1 million. These findings are consistent with previous research on demographics and financial decision-making, which suggests that women and older adults tend to be more risk-averse than men and younger adults.

The survey's findings have significant implications for how financial institutions and policymakers communicate with the public about financial risks and rewards. For example, the results suggest that people may be more responsive to messages that emphasize the certainty of a financial outcome, rather than the potential for large gains. The survey's findings also highlight the importance of financial education and literacy, particularly among women and younger adults, who may be more vulnerable to financial risks due to their preferences for certainty. The results of the survey have been welcomed by financial experts, who see them as an important contribution to our understanding of financial decision-making.

The survey's findings are also relevant to the broader debate about risk and uncertainty in financial markets. The results suggest that people's preferences for certainty over chance are not limited to individual financial decisions, but may also influence their attitudes towards risk and uncertainty more generally. This has significant implications for how policymakers and regulators approach issues such as financial stability and consumer protection. The survey's findings also highlight the importance of considering the psychological and emotional factors that drive financial decision-making, rather than simply focusing on economic or financial factors.

As the survey's findings are digested by policymakers and financial experts, it is likely that there will be a renewed focus on how to communicate financial risks and rewards to the public in a way that takes account of people's preferences for certainty. This may involve the development of new financial products or services that offer greater certainty and stability, or the creation of education and awareness campaigns that help people to better understand financial risks and rewards. Whatever the outcome, the survey's findings are an important reminder of the complex and multifaceted nature of financial decision-making, and the need for policymakers and financial experts to take account of the psychological and emotional factors that drive human behavior.

items.headline: Britain's driest areas face prolonged drought as next heatwave looms on the horizon.
items.teaser: Parts of the United Kingdom that are experiencing severe drought have missed an opportunity for significant rainfall, with forecasters pr…
items.story:
Parts of the United Kingdom that are experiencing severe drought have missed an opportunity for significant rainfall, with forecasters predicting another heatwave in the coming days. The country's southern and eastern regions, which have been particularly affected by the dry conditions, saw only light and scattered showers over the past week. Meteorologists had hoped that a low-pressure system would bring more substantial rainfall to these areas, but it ultimately passed to the north, bringing rain to parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland instead. As a result, water levels in reservoirs and rivers remain low, and farmers are struggling to maintain their crops.

The UK's dry spell began earlier this summer, with June and July seeing significantly below-average rainfall in many areas. This has led to a surge in water usage, with many households and businesses relying on hosepipe bans to conserve water. The dry conditions have also had a major impact on agriculture, with crop yields expected to be lower than usual and farmers facing significant financial losses. The UK's National Farmers' Union has warned that the drought could have long-term consequences for the country's food production and security. Historically, the UK's climate has been characterized by mild and wet conditions, but in recent years, the country has experienced more frequent and severe heatwaves.

According to data from the UK's Met Office, some parts of the country have seen less than 50% of their average rainfall over the past three months. The agency has also issued a level 3 heatwave alert, indicating that the heatwave is likely to have significant impacts on health, transport, and other services. The Environment Agency has reported that river levels are at a 20-year low in some areas, and groundwater levels are also depleted. Experts warn that the dry conditions could persist into the autumn, with potential consequences for the UK's ecosystems and wildlife.

The lack of rainfall has sparked concerns among residents, farmers, and business owners, who are calling for more support from the government to mitigate the effects of the drought. Many are also taking steps to conserve water, such as installing rainwater harvesting systems and reducing their water usage. The UK's water companies have implemented hosepipe bans and other restrictions to reduce demand, but some critics argue that more needs to be done to address the root causes of the drought. The government has announced plans to provide financial support to farmers and other affected businesses, but the details of the package have yet to be finalized.

The UK's drought is part of a larger pattern of extreme weather events affecting Europe and other parts of the world. Climate change is widely seen as a major contributor to these events, with rising temperatures and changing precipitation patterns altering the likelihood and severity of heatwaves and droughts. The UK's experience is being closely watched by other countries, which are also grappling with the challenges of adapting to a changing climate. International cooperation and knowledge-sharing will be crucial in addressing the global implications of drought and heatwaves, and in developing effective strategies for mitigating their impacts.

As the UK prepares for another heatwave, attention is turning to the measures that can be taken to reduce the risks associated with extreme weather events. The government is under pressure to develop a more comprehensive strategy for addressing drought and water scarcity, including investing in water infrastructure and promoting water conservation. In the short term, residents and businesses are being advised to take precautions to stay safe and minimize their water usage, with the Met Office warning that the heatwave could persist for several days. The UK's experience serves as a reminder of the need for vigilance and preparedness in the face of a rapidly changing climate.

items.headline: Research Suggests Controlled Blazes May be Key to Preserving Ancient Giant Sequoia Ecosystems
items.teaser: Researchers in California have found that giant sequoias, some of which have survived for millennia, may have a better chance of survival…
items.story:
Researchers in California have found that giant sequoias, some of which have survived for millennia, may have a better chance of survival in the face of extreme wildfires if they are exposed to controlled fires. This discovery comes after a recent analysis of approximately 26,400 sequoias revealed that trees in areas treated with prescribed burns were nearly four times more likely to survive. The study's findings suggest that the use of controlled fires could be a crucial tool in protecting these ancient trees from the devastating effects of wildfires. Giant sequoias are built to withstand ordinary fires, but recent extreme wildfires have killed thousands of trees that had stood for centuries.

The giant sequoia is one of the most resilient tree species in the world, with some individuals estimated to be over 3,000 years old. However, the increasing frequency and severity of wildfires in recent years have posed a significant threat to their survival. The 2019-2020 wildfire season in California was particularly devastating, with thousands of giant sequoias killed in a single fire. This has led to a renewed focus on finding effective ways to protect these trees, and the use of prescribed burns is being explored as a potential solution. By understanding the history and ecology of giant sequoias, researchers can better appreciate the importance of preserving these natural wonders.

The analysis of the 26,400 sequoias found that the controlled fires prevented approximately 1,900 deaths, and it is estimated that thousands more could have been saved if this technique had been used across every grove. The study's authors suggest that the use of prescribed burns can help to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires by clearing away dead and dying vegetation that can fuel large fires. This approach is not without its risks, however, and careful planning and management are required to ensure that the controlled fires do not get out of control. According to experts, the key to successful prescribed burns is to carefully consider factors such as weather conditions, fuel loads, and the location of sensitive habitats.

The findings of the study have been welcomed by conservationists and forestry experts, who see the use of prescribed burns as a valuable tool in the fight to protect giant sequoias. The US Forest Service has already begun to incorporate prescribed burns into its management plans for giant sequoia groves, and other organizations are likely to follow suit. While there are still many challenges to overcome, the use of controlled fires offers a glimmer of hope for the long-term survival of these incredible trees. As the world continues to grapple with the impacts of climate change, the preservation of giant sequoias is an important reminder of the need to protect our natural heritage.

The use of prescribed burns to protect giant sequoias is part of a broader effort to rethink the way that wildfires are managed in the western United States. In recent years, there has been a growing recognition of the importance of allowing natural fires to burn in certain areas, rather than seeking to suppress them at all costs. This approach, known as "fire management," acknowledges that fire is a natural part of many ecosystems, and that it can play a crucial role in maintaining the health and diversity of these systems. By embracing this approach, land managers can help to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires, while also promoting the long-term health of forests and other ecosystems.

As researchers and land managers continue to explore the use of prescribed burns to protect giant sequoias, there are likely to be many challenges and uncertainties ahead. One of the key questions that remains to be answered is how to balance the need to protect these trees with the need to allow natural fires to burn in certain areas. Additionally, there will be a need to carefully monitor the impacts of prescribed burns on the broader ecosystem, and to make adjustments as necessary. Despite these challenges, the use of controlled fires offers a promising approach to protecting giant sequoias, and it is likely to play an increasingly important role in the management of these incredible trees in the years to come.

items.story:
As the United States grapples with an increasingly strained power grid, a potential solution may be sitting in many American driveways, in the form of electric vehicles capable of providing backup power. The number of these vehicles, often referred to as vehicle-to-grid, or V2G, models, is growing rapidly, with several major automakers now offering them as an option. This development comes at a time when the US is in need of innovative solutions to meet its rising electricity demands. With the country's power infrastructure facing numerous challenges, from aging equipment to extreme weather events, the ability of electric vehicles to supply backup power could play a significant role in stabilizing the grid.

The concept of using electric vehicles as a source of backup power is not new, but recent advancements in technology have made it more viable and efficient. Historically, the power grid has been a one-way system, with electricity flowing from power plants to consumers, but the rise of renewable energy sources and energy storage technologies has enabled the development of a more dynamic and flexible grid. As the US continues to transition towards cleaner energy sources, the need for innovative solutions to manage the grid and ensure a stable supply of electricity has become more pressing. The growing adoption of electric vehicles, with their advanced battery systems, has created an opportunity to utilize these vehicles as a distributed energy resource, helping to balance the grid and provide backup power during outages.

According to industry experts, the number of electric vehicles capable of providing V2G power is expected to increase significantly in the coming years, with several major automakers investing heavily in the development of this technology. For example, companies like Ford and General Motors have announced plans to integrate V2G capabilities into their electric vehicle models, while startups like Fermata Energy are working on developing the necessary software and hardware to enable this functionality. Data from the US Department of Energy suggests that widespread adoption of V2G technology could provide enough backup power to support millions of homes, helping to alleviate strain on the grid during peak demand periods.

The potential impact of V2G technology on the US power grid is significant, and stakeholders are taking notice. Utility companies, in particular, are expressing interest in the technology, as it could provide a new tool for managing peak demand and reducing strain on the grid. Additionally, the ability of electric vehicles to provide backup power during outages could have a major impact on public safety, particularly in areas prone to extreme weather events. As the technology continues to develop, it is likely that we will see increased collaboration between automakers, utility companies, and government agencies to integrate V2G capabilities into the grid.

The development of V2G technology is part of a broader trend towards the electrification of transportation and the integration of renewable energy sources into the grid. As countries around the world transition towards cleaner energy sources, the need for innovative solutions to manage the grid and ensure a stable supply of electricity is becoming increasingly pressing. The US is not alone in exploring the potential of V2G technology, with countries like Japan and the UK also investing in the development of this technology. As the global energy landscape continues to evolve, it is likely that we will see increased adoption of V2G technology, as well as other innovative solutions aimed at stabilizing the grid and reducing our reliance on fossil fuels.

As the US continues to develop and deploy V2G technology, several key questions remain to be answered, including how to integrate these systems into the existing grid infrastructure and how to ensure the safety and reliability of the technology. Additionally, there are ongoing debates about the potential impact of V2G technology on electric vehicle battery lifespan and the overall cost-effectiveness of the technology. As these questions are addressed, it is likely that we will see increased adoption of V2G technology, and a growing recognition of the potential for electric vehicles to play a key role in stabilizing the US power grid.

The United States has revised its casualty figures from the recent conflict with Iran, reducing the reported death toll from 18 to 14, according to a recent announcement from the Pentagon. This change in reporting comes after the department altered its methodology for tracking casualties, a move that has drawn criticism from lawmakers who accuse the Trump administration of decreasing transparency. The revised figures were released after a thorough review of the incident, which occurred earlier this year. The Pentagon's decision to reclassify certain injuries has contributed to the reduction in reported deaths.

The conflict between the US and Iran has been a major point of contention in recent months, with tensions escalating after a US drone strike killed a top Iranian military commander. The incident sparked a retaliatory strike from Iran, which targeted US military bases in Iraq. The US initially reported 18 casualties, but the new figures suggest that the number of deaths was lower than initially thought. The revision has raised questions about the accuracy of initial reports and the methods used to track casualties. The incident has also highlighted the ongoing tensions between the US and Iran, which have been a major concern for regional stability.

According to Pentagon officials, the revised figures are the result of a thorough review of the incident, which included an assessment of the injuries sustained by US personnel. The officials stated that certain injuries were reclassified, which contributed to the reduction in reported deaths. The Pentagon has also changed its methodology for tracking casualties, which will affect how future incidents are reported. The new approach is intended to provide a more accurate picture of the number of casualties, but critics argue that it reduces transparency. The Pentagon has not provided further details on the revised methodology, citing operational security concerns.

Lawmakers have criticized the Trump administration for reducing transparency in its reporting of casualties, arguing that the revised figures are an attempt to downplay the severity of the incident. Critics also argue that the change in methodology will make it more difficult to track casualties in the future, which could undermine accountability. The revision has also sparked concerns about the accuracy of initial reports and the potential for similar incidents to be underreported. The incident has highlighted the need for greater transparency in reporting casualties, particularly in conflicts where the US is involved. The reaction from lawmakers reflects the ongoing debate about the US role in the region and the need for greater accountability.

The revised casualty figures are part of a broader context of ongoing tensions between the US and Iran, which have been exacerbated by recent incidents. The conflict has raised concerns about regional stability and the potential for further escalation. The US has maintained a significant military presence in the region, which has been a point of contention with Iran. The incident has also highlighted the need for greater diplomacy and dialogue to reduce tensions and prevent further conflict. The international community has called for restraint and a return to diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict peacefully. The US and Iran have been engaged in a war of words, with each side accusing the other of aggression.

The revision of casualty figures and the change in methodology for tracking casualties will likely be the subject of further debate and scrutiny in the coming weeks. Lawmakers will likely press the Pentagon for more information on the revised methodology and the factors that contributed to the reduction in reported deaths. The incident has also raised questions about the US role in the region and the potential for further conflict. items.story: 'ആലപ്പുഴയിലെ കോൺഗ്രസ്-CPM കൂട്ടുകെട്ട് അവസാനിപ്പിക്കണം'; ചെന്നിത്തലയെ വേദിയിലിരുത്തി ജി. സുധാകരൻ Mathrubhumi‘സിപിഎമ്മിലെ ചിലരുമായുള്ള കൂട്ടുകച്ചവടം അവസാനിപ്പിക്കണം’; ചെന്നിത്തലയെ വേദിയിലിരുത്തി ജി.സുധാകരന്റെ വിമർശനം Manorama Onlineവേദിയിൽ രമേശ് ചെന്നിത്തല, കോൺഗ്രസിനെതിരെ തുറന്നടിച്ച് ജി സുധാകരൻ; സിപിഎം കൂട്ടുക്കെട്ട് എന്ന് ആരോപണം, മറുപടിയുമായി ആഭ്യന്തര മന്ത്രി Asianet News Malayalam'എന്നെ ഒറ്റപ്പെടുത്താൻ ഗൂഢാലോചന'; ചെന്നിത്തലയെ സാക്ഷിയാക്കി സിപിഎമ്മിനെതിരെ ജി സുധാകരന്റെ തുറന്നാക്രമണം Mangalamചെന

items.story: The fossilized spines of saber-toothed cats in the La Brea Tar Pits reveal evidence of an unexpectedly high prevalence of rare spinal nerve tumors, suggesting that the species became inbred just before extinction. These tumors, which cause significant pain and reduced limb function, could have made the cats particularly vulnerable to the lure of prey animals stuck in the tar pits.

A Josephson junction—two superconductors separated by an ultrathin barrier—can turn a voltage into a quantum oscillation with extraordinary precision. Would intense gravity change that quantum rule, or only change how a faraway observer reads the device?

items.headline: Twisted laser light distinguishes mirror-image molecules by their fragment counts
items.teaser: Many molecules exist in two mirror-image forms—like left and right hands—that look identical but can behave very differently, especially …
items.story: Many molecules exist in two mirror-image forms—like left and right hands—that look identical but can behave very differently, especially in biological systems and pharmaceuticals. Distinguishing between these enantiomers (also called chiral molecules) is a longstanding challenge in science and technology. A useful analogy is that of a screw and a nut: A right-handed screw fits only into a right-handed thread, while a left-handed one will not engage properly.

items.headline: When a teenager makes the 'stupid choice,' their brain is working exactly as designed
items.teaser: When an adult refuses to let an injustice pass—stands up to a bully or asserts their rights—we call it principle. When a 15-year-old reta…
items.story: When an adult refuses to let an injustice pass—stands up to a bully or asserts their rights—we call it principle. When a 15-year-old retaliates to an insult thrown in a school corridor, risking detention, we call it a failure to think ahead. It's easy to ascribe this to a not-yet-developed teenage brain: a convenient shorthand for assuming they simply cannot weigh consequences properly.

items.story: By analyzing the data from NASA's Fermi gamma-ray space telescope, Chinese astronomers have investigated a recently identified millisecond pulsar known as PSR J0435+3233. As a result, they found that the pulsar exhibits gamma-ray pulsations. The discovery was detailed in a paper published July 17 on the pre-print server arXiv.

items.headline: The best way to save giant sequoias may be more fire
items.teaser: Giant sequoias are built to withstand ordinary fires, but recent extreme wildfires killed thousands of trees that had survived for centur…
items.story: Giant sequoias are built to withstand ordinary fires, but recent extreme wildfires killed thousands of trees that had survived for centuries or even millennia. A new analysis of about 26,400 sequoias found that trees in areas treated with prescribed burns were nearly four times more likely to survive. Researchers estimate the controlled fires prevented about 1,900 deaths and could have saved thousands more if used across every grove.

items.headline: The internet’s creepiest place is becoming a tourist attraction
items.teaser: The Backrooms began as a single eerie image of empty yellow rooms, but internet users transformed it into a vast fictional world that fee…
items.story: The Backrooms began as a single eerie image of empty yellow rooms, but internet users transformed it into a vast fictional world that feels disturbingly real. Through videos, games, maps, survival guides and social media stories, audiences do more than watch the horror unfold. They help build and explore it. Researchers suggest this popularity reflects a new kind of digital tourism, where people emotionally enter imaginary places filled with mystery, nostalgia and unease.

items.headline: Hidden genetic diversity helped inbred brown tree snakes conquer guam
items.teaser: A notorious snake invasion that devastated Guam’s native birds may have succeeded because the reptiles carried hidden genetic advantages.…
items.story: A notorious snake invasion that devastated Guam’s native birds may have succeeded because the reptiles carried hidden genetic advantages. Using advanced long-read DNA sequencing, researchers uncovered more than 19,000 large genetic differences in brown tree snakes, many concentrated in genes tied to immunity and smell. This overlooked diversity may have helped a population founded by only a few snakes survive inbreeding, adapt to a new environment, and multiply to extraordinary densities.

items.story: Researchers say a tiny one-eyed ancestor that lived nearly 600 million years ago may have shaped the evolution of every vertebrate eye, including our own. They also found that its ancient median eye lives on today as the pineal gland, which helps synchronize our sleep with daylight.

Eventually, accelerating expansion will push nearly every galaxy beyond our Local Group out of sight, making the Universe appear almost empty.

items.story: Newer oral drugs related to semaglutide medications such as Ozempic reduced pleasure-driven eating in mice by quieting a deep brain reward circuit. The finding could open new avenues for understanding food cravings and potentially treating substance use disorder.

items.headline: Venus may be tearing itself apart from within
items.teaser: Scientists have uncovered new evidence that Venus may still be tearing itself apart from within. Advanced 3D simulations indicate that so…
items.story: Scientists have uncovered new evidence that Venus may still be tearing itself apart from within. Advanced 3D simulations indicate that some of the planet's giant rift valleys formed relatively recently and could still be expanding. The results suggest Venus has a far more active interior than researchers once believed, challenging the long-held view of a geologically dormant world.

items.headline: Scientists discover the Sun contains 55% more silver than expected
items.teaser: A new analysis suggests the Sun holds far more silver than earlier estimates indicated. More advanced models of the solar atmosphere rais…
items.story: A new analysis suggests the Sun holds far more silver than earlier estimates indicated. More advanced models of the solar atmosphere raised the calculated amount by 55 percent, bringing it into much closer agreement with ancient meteorites. The technique may also help scientists track the cosmic origins of silver and other heavy elements.
